facts.summary: Missouri's minimum wage is $15.00 per hour effective January 1, 2026, higher than the federal $7.25.
facts.sourceAgency: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations
facts.notes: Per HB 567 (2025), the wage is no longer annually adjusted by CPI. Tipped employees must be paid at least 50% ($7.50/hr) plus enough to reach full minimum wage.

facts.summary: Missouri requires overtime at 1.5x after 40 hours per week and incorporates the FLSA's exemptions; there is no daily overtime or higher salary floor.
facts.notes: Statute is interpreted in accordance with the FLSA (29 U.S.C. 201 et seq.). Exception: certain amusement/recreation businesses owe OT only after 52 hours/week.

facts.summary: The Missouri Human Rights Act prohibits employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, disability, and age.
facts.notes: Age is protected in employment only. Sexual orientation and gender identity are not enumerated in the MHRA. Age coverage under MHRA is broader than federal ADEA's 40+/20-employee limits but verify age-range specifics.

facts.summary: The Missouri Human Rights Act covers employers with six or more employees, a lower threshold than Title VII's 15.
facts.notes: Six or more employees for each working day in 20+ calendar weeks in the current or preceding year. Excludes corporations/associations owned or operated by religious or sectarian organizations.

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the Missouri Commission on Human Rights within 180 days of the alleged discriminatory act.
facts.notes: Failure to timely file deprives the commission of jurisdiction. This is shorter than the federal 300-day cross-filing window in deferral states.

facts.summary: Missouri's Whistleblower's Protection Act makes it unlawful to discharge an employee for reporting or refusing to carry out an unlawful act, providing actual (not punitive) damages.
facts.notes: Enacted 2017; codifies and limits the common-law public-policy exception to at-will employment. Applies to at-will employees; provides a private right of action for actual damages but not punitive damages.

facts.summary: An action to collect unpaid minimum wages or overtime must be brought within three years of accrual.
facts.notes: Recovery includes the unpaid wages plus an additional amount equal to twice the unpaid wages as liquidated damages, costs, and attorney fees.
